newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SUZUKI TO UP CAR OUTPUT 4.0 PCT IN HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: SUZUKI TO UP CAR OUTPUT 4.0 PCT IN HUNGARY.

text.p: Japanese automaker Suzuki Motor Corp said on Thursday it planned to increase its car production in Hungary to 54,000 units in 1997 from 52,000 units in 1996, according to Hungarian news agency MTI.
Suzuki said its output in Hungary could increase 10,000 a year in coming years, but offered no additional details, MTI reported.
The Hungarian plant, which exported 70 percent of its output in 1996, will export all of its additional 2,000 units of output in 1997, MTI reported.
Magyar Suzuki Rt, the name of the Hungarian company, reported its first profit in 1996, earning 887 million forints on revenue of 56.7 billion forints, MTI reported.
It was unclear whether the profits were gross or net, but the Hungarian government granted Magyar Suzuki tax concessions in connection with its investment.

Magyar Suzuki, which has built and sold Suzuki Swift hatchbacks and sedans since 1992, planned to invest 2.5 billion forints in 1997, mainly to open a parts warehouse and to boost the amount of domestic supplies in its cars, MTI reported.
